ANSWER: The decision lives in `src/memory/guard.rs`. The function `secret_kind(text: &str) -> Option<&'static str>` decides whether a piece of text looks like a secret: it first tests the text against the `SECRETS` regex table (private keys, AWS/GitHub/Slack/Stripe/etc. tokens, JWTs, password assignments), and if none match, it scans for long base64-ish runs with the `LONG_TOKEN` regex (`[A-Za-z0-9+/_=-]{32,}`) and reports a "high-entropy token". The helper that tells random-looking tokens apart from hashes/ids is `looks_random(token: &str) -> bool` in the same file — it requires mixed lowercase/uppercase/digit characters and computes Shannon entropy per byte, returning true only when entropy exceeds 4.2 (so hex/base32 hashes and ids pass, base64 keys don't). The caller `check_secret` (also in `guard.rs`) invokes `secret_kind` and turns a match into a `Refused` error; `check` runs `check_secret` on each field.
